newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria moves to speed up bank privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria moves to speed up bank privatisation.

text.p: Bulgaria's government on Monday boosted its presence on the board of the Bank Consolidation Co (BCC) in a bid to speed up bank sell-offs, Finance Minister Muravei Radev said.
"The government increased its representation on the board to speed up bank privatisation," Radev said.
The BCC manages state equity in local commercial banks.

The BCC extraordinary shareholders' meeting on Monday elected deputy finance minister Plamen Oresharski as a board member. Radev and deputy Prime Minister Alexander Bozhkov also sit on the five-member board.
The shareholders also elected Petar Zhotev and the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) deputy governor Emilia Milanova as board members, Radev said.
The three new board members replaced the former BCC executive director Valentin Tsvetanov, who has become a BNB deputy governor in June, and Dimitar Dimitrov and Zdravko Balyozov from the BNB.

Petar Zhotev was appointed as a BCC executive director. He has been a senior manager at the Sofia office of Ernst & Young's Banks and Corporate Finance Team and has worked for the World Bank in Sofia and for the Bulgarian National Bank (BNB).
The BNB holds some 48 percent of the BCC, the government has around 51 percent and Sofia Municipality one percent.
Last week the BCC sealed Bulgaria's first bank privatisation deal, selling its 99.6 percent stake in the United Bulgarian Bank to the EBRD, Bulgaria's Bulbank and U.S. Oppenheimer & Co.
Bulgaria hopes to privatise all its remaining five state banks by mid-1998. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
